line: e4 Nf6 Qh5 c5 Qxc5 Nxe4 Qh5 Nc6
teaches: Against an early queen sortie, develop at the centre rather than hunting the queen — every piece that comes out with a job keeps the queen short of safe squares by itself.
explains: Against an early queen sortie, don't hunt the queen — develop at the centre. The knight to c6 covers d4 and puts a second piece out, while White's queen has already moved three times and holds nothing. Chase it directly and you'd burn your own tempo; this keeps every move useful, and the queen still has to find somewhere to stand.

line: e4 Nf6 Qh5 c5 Qxc5 Nxe4 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 e6 Qf3 d5
teaches: The best central pawn move is the one that arrives hitting something — when a single push both builds the centre and gains a move, it is nearly always the move.
explains: The best central push is the one that arrives hitting something. The pawn to d5 attacks the bishop on c4 and claims the centre in the same move, so the bishop has to spend a move retreating and the centre gets built for free. Look for this whenever an enemy piece sits on a diagonal a pawn can reach.
